concurrency.title: One stale writer commits, the other conflicts
concurrency.summary: Both local threads read version zero; a barrier ensures the race precondition. The winning thread is unspecified.

nodes.label: Both read v0
nodes.description: Two proposals use the same old version.

nodes.label: Barrier
nodes.description: Neither updates before both have read.

nodes.label: Locked compare/write
nodes.description: Only one thread owns the critical section at a time.

nodes.label: One commit -> v1
nodes.description: The first valid proposal increments version.

nodes.label: Stale proposal rejected
nodes.description: The second expected version zero no longer matches.

steps.title: Establish shared old version
steps.explanation: The barrier creates the material precondition without choosing a winner.

steps.title: Commit one proposal
steps.explanation: Comparison and update occur under the same local lock.

steps.title: Reject the stale proposal
steps.explanation: Assert one success, one conflict and version one; do not require a particular thread to win.

integration-files.title: Validate before replacing the report
integration-files.summary: A complete batch is checked before any replacement; a failure must preserve old output.

nodes.label: Batch input
nodes.description: Synthetic JSON lines with a bound.

nodes.label: Validate all rows
nodes.description: Fields, types and duplicate IDs checked.

nodes.label: Temporary report
nodes.description: Serialization and flush in destination directory.

nodes.label: Replace once
nodes.description: Publish the complete local report.

nodes.label: Failure branch
nodes.description: Keep old bytes and clean temporary artifacts.

steps.title: Reject before effects
steps.explanation: Validation failure never invokes replacement.

steps.title: Prepare complete bytes
steps.explanation: The target remains old while a temporary report is built.

steps.title: Publish or clean up
steps.explanation: Real replacement is tested separately from an injected failure; this is not multi-writer coordination.

reproduce.title: Reduction must preserve the failure condition
reproduce.summary: The duplicate-ID example shrinks 1000 rows to two matching IDs. Removing a material row makes the failure disappear.

nodes.label: Recorded failure
nodes.description: Exact command, runtime, expected result and observed failure.

nodes.label: Large input
nodes.description: 1000 synthetic rows reproduce the defect.

nodes.label: Two duplicate rows
nodes.description: Reduce unrelated data while retaining ID a twice.

nodes.label: One row removed
nodes.description: The duplicate condition is no longer present.

nodes.label: Failure disappears
nodes.description: The changed observation identifies a material condition.

nodes.label: Minimal reproduction note
nodes.description: Share the remaining fixture and explicit expected/observed outcomes.

steps.title: Capture before reducing
steps.explanation: Synthetic versioned input makes the failure repeatable without live private data.

steps.title: Test what is material
steps.explanation: Failure disappearing after one duplicate row is removed supports a uniqueness-boundary hypothesis.

steps.title: Keep the failing fixture
steps.explanation: The final note preserves the two-row failure, command and runtime; it does not keep the nonfailing reduction as the reproducer.

hypotheses.title: Make a prediction that an observation can disprove
hypotheses.summary: The guided diagnosis contract includes index stop. For [4,8,16] with stop 1, the expected sum is independently 12.

nodes.label: Contract and input
nodes.description: Sum indexes zero through stop; expected 12.

nodes.label: Observed mutant result
nodes.description: The deliberate mutant prints 4.

nodes.label: Boundary hypothesis
nodes.description: Suspect an exclusive slice endpoint.

nodes.label: Debugger observation
nodes.description: values[:stop] is [4], omitting the needed 8.

nodes.label: Correction and regression
nodes.description: Include stop+1 and assert an independent expected result.

steps.title: State the mismatch
steps.explanation: Keep the agreed contract separate from current arithmetic.

steps.title: Choose a discriminating observation
steps.explanation: A breakpoint is useful when it answers a concrete question about input and chosen branch.

steps.title: Preserve the corrected behavior
steps.explanation: The regression distinguishes the mutant from the fix; changing only the printed message does not repair the function.

async-debugging.title: Cancel after acquisition and observe cleanup
async-debugging.summary: The guided kit uses an event to establish readiness. The timeout is a hang guard; it does not order the tasks.

nodes.label: Resource acquired
nodes.description: Child owns the synthetic resource.

nodes.label: Started event
nodes.description: Signals acquisition before cancellation.

nodes.label: Parent cancels
nodes.description: Cancel only after readiness is observed.

nodes.label: Cancellation cleanup
nodes.description: The cancelled child's finally appends released exactly once before cancellation propagates.

nodes.label: Caller observes cancellation
nodes.description: Await propagates CancelledError and no commit.

nodes.label: Successful work commits
nodes.description: Without cancellation, the child records committed before leaving the body.

nodes.label: Success cleanup
nodes.description: The successful child's finally also appends released exactly once.

nodes.label: Caller observes success
nodes.description: Await finishes normally; assert both committed and released markers.

steps.title: Establish acquisition
steps.explanation: The started event avoids racing cancellation against startup.

steps.title: Observe cancellation and cleanup
steps.explanation: Assert cancellation propagation, no committed marker and exactly one released marker.

steps.title: Check the success path too
steps.explanation: The separate successful case records committed, runs finally to record released, then finishes normally. It does not raise CancelledError. This local resource test does not prove process-kill or repeated-cancellation cleanup.

coverage.title: A reached line can still miss a discriminating boundary
coverage.summary: The lesson changes <=1440 to <1440. Both tests execute the comparison, but only the endpoint reveals the altered contract.

nodes.label: Duration contract
nodes.description: 1440 is valid; 1441 is invalid.

nodes.label: Altered comparison
nodes.description: Mutant rejects exactly 1440.

nodes.label: Ordinary case 30
nodes.description: Passes both original and mutant.

nodes.label: Boundary case 1440
nodes.description: Expected acceptance distinguishes the mutant.

nodes.label: Observed evidence
nodes.description: Record which assertion fails; coverage alone reports execution.

steps.title: Name the altered rule
steps.explanation: A controlled mutation asks whether assertions protect the actual contract.

steps.title: Compare the two cases
steps.explanation: 30 reaches the comparison but misses the changed endpoint; 1440 exposes it.

steps.title: Interpret evidence narrowly
steps.explanation: Line coverage cannot tell these tests apart. One caught mutant is not a universal quality score.

strategy.title: Choose test scope for the observable risk
strategy.summary: The importer example needs parser, filesystem and command-route evidence. A future browser interface introduces another boundary.

nodes.label: Risk: corrupt report
nodes.description: Invalid rows must not replace the saved report.

nodes.label: Unit parser test
nodes.description: Control input classes and assert rejection.

nodes.label: Integration file test
nodes.description: Use real collaborators and verify old bytes survive.

nodes.label: Complete local CLI route
nodes.description: Observe actual process output and exit status.

nodes.label: Future browser route
nodes.description: UI effects need a component or browser test.

nodes.label: Evidence limits
nodes.description: Each passing scope leaves other product boundaries unproved.

steps.title: Test the small behavior
steps.explanation: Parser tests cover types quickly but cannot observe browser rendering or persisted output.

steps.title: Cross real collaborators
steps.explanation: File readback checks storage effects; mocks need separate real-boundary checks.

steps.title: Exercise the actual route
steps.explanation: A local subprocess verifies the command route, while a stale-response UI bug needs its actual component/browser boundary.
